solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Love fictional genre

definitions.meaning: a love affair, an amorous relationship
the kind of novel about love stories, as published by Mills & Boon

explanation.surface: A reader declares a passion for one particular kind of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a love affair and the literary genre of love stories, so each half of the clue is a sense.

clue.text: We are weird, extremely dense idiots that need to be managed

indicators.note: letters that need to be managed are to be organised into a new order
extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word dense

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of oddballs confesses that thick fools like them need someone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes DE, the outer letters of 'dense'; 'need to be managed' rearranges DE with IDIOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or peculiar things and people are curiosities, so a speaker who is one of them could say they are weird.

clue.text: As Paddington Station's entrance is covered in wee

indicators.note: covered in means the letter is wrapped by the other word

parts.note: wee is slang for urine

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter, here taken from Station's

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a London railway station's entrance soiled with urine.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is the fictional bear, so 'As Paddington' means bear-like; 'Paddington Station' is a London terminus, which disguises it. 'covered in' puts S inside URINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or resembling bears, and Paddington is a famous storybook bear.

clue.text: Reportedly sterilise — wise these days

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to spay is to sterilise a female animal, and sage means wise: together, spay sage

explanation.surface: A wise remark that sterilisation is the done thing nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' says SPAY SAGE spoken sounds like the phrase entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern era of rockets and technology is a jokey label for the present time we live in.

clue.text: Valuer regularly raised charge for Roman coin

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of Valuer, here the second, fourth and sixth
in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to sue is to charge someone in court

explanation.surface: An appraiser lifts the price on an ancient Roman coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes AUR from Valuer; 'raised' turns SUE upwards to give EUS.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the gold coin of ancient Rome, so it is a type of Roman money.

clue.text: Former statesman, drunk in style?

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether a past politician was famously drunk with some panache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges IN STYLE; the question mark nods to the Russian leader's well-known fondness for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first President of Russia, a former head of state and politician.

clue.text: Food is fine, given more rum

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
rum means odd, so more rum is odder

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the meal is good and better still with extra rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is British slang for strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal feed such as hay is food for livestock; the word also means material simply consumed.

clue.text: Sport training sure jiggled busts

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union, a sport
PT is physical training

indicators.note: jiggled means the letters of sure are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Sports bras: training jiggles the bust, so support matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jiggled' rearranges SURE into URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Busts as a noun are breaks or bursts, as in hernias or burst pipes; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: To a tee, British nuts react when provoked

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Exactly as expected, mad Brits react when wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges all the letters of TO A TEE and BRITISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from fishing, means to respond to taunting or provocation exactly as intended.

clue.text: Entitles one to stop false ID being processed

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so this letter goes into the middle of the others
being processed means the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A bureaucratic tale: a fake ID being processed lets one claim an entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being processed' rearranges FALSE ID; 'to stop' puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a lady of someone is to confer a title on her, so the verb fits giving a title.

clue.text: A sequence of rescues targeted steep ridge

indicators.note: sequence of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A series of mountain rescues aimed at a sharp hillside ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical term for a ridge with a gentle slope on one side and a steep scarp on the other.

clue.text: Old detectives finding US money around the west

indicators.note: around means the money goes round the detectives

parts.note: a cent is a US coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Veteran detectives discover American cash all around the West.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the western world, Europe and the Americas, as opposed to the Orient.

clue.text: Capital of a country from which broken artist has departed

indicators.note: has departed means these letters leave the longer word

parts.note: Austrian means of the country Austria
RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist; broken means its two letters are split apart

explanation.surface: A capital city in a country that a failed painter has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' says R and A are not together: R and A leave AUSTRIAN separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin is the capital city of the US state of Texas, once itself an independent republic.

clue.text: Mixes rank soldiers, in a way, while touring

indicators.note: touring means going around, so these letters wrap the rest

parts.note: as means while, in the sense of during

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
rank means class or kind, which is sort
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers on the road, joining up while touring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixes' is a plural noun here, not a verb; 'rank' is a class or kind, not a row of soldiers. The lone 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Collections of various different things are mixtures, plural noun to plural noun.

clue.text: Earwig in England, in your ear?

indicators.note: in your ear means the phrase is heard rather than seen

parts.note: an American in England would say they are over here

explanation.surface: An insect question: is there an earwig in England, crawling in your ear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earwig' is a verb here, informal British for eavesdrop, not the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for to listen secretly to someone else's conversation, to eavesdrop.

clue.text: State of euphoria, perhaps after exam is put back

indicators.note: after places the excitement after the exam
is put back means the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: SAT is a standard test, an exam
mania is a state of wild excitement, of which euphoria is an example

explanation.surface: Elation follows when an exam is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put back' turns SAT into TAS. 'State' is the Australian sense, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia, one of its six constituent states.

clue.text: British under pressure to find alternate culinary plant

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts this letter below the rest

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
other means alternate, as in every other day

explanation.surface: A British cook under pressure seeks a substitute herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is any plant grown for cooking, such as a leafy vegetable or seasoning.

clue.text: Half-heartedly piled bananas into empty tummy

indicators.note: into puts the jumbled letters inside the emptied word
empty means remove the inside, leaving only the outer letters of tummy
bananas means crazy, so the letters go mad into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone without enthusiasm stuffs a heap of bananas into an empty tummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is the anagram signal, not fruit: the jumbled letters of PILED go inside the emptied tummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm in feeling, without enthusiasm, is the sense of the adverb, matching half-hearted effort.

clue.text: Posh stole redesigned as ruffle

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are made into a new pattern

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
taken as written

explanation.surface: A posh shawl is remade as a frilly ruffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges U with STOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle hair is to tangle or dishevel it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Copper shouted farewell

indicators.note: shouted means the letters are spoken aloud as sounds

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman calls out goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, giving its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual parting phrase meaning goodbye until next time.

clue.text: Got help through having heard, getting somewhat moved

indicators.note: somewhat moved means part of the word shifts to a new place

parts.note: listened means having heard

explanation.surface: Someone finds help after hearing something rather touching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat moved' shifts EN from the middle of LISTENED to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist someone's aid is to obtain their help, as in enlisting a friend's support.

clue.text: Tramp's shoe

explanation.surface: A vagrant's footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an idler who does no work and also a slip-on leather shoe without laces.

clue.text: Flail two thirds of verge

indicators.note: two thirds of keeps the opening six of the nine letters, dropping the final three

parts.note: verge means a brink or entrance edge, a doorway sill

explanation.surface: Swinging wildly on the edge, two-thirds of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A flail is the tool for beating grain from its husk, and to use one is to beat corn.

clue.text: Farewell amid brief pivotal tranquillity

indicators.note: amid puts the goodbye inside the other word
brief means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: axial means pivotal, relating to an axis
ta-ra is an informal northern English goodbye

explanation.surface: A goodbye in the middle of a short, crucial moment of calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ra is an informal goodbye from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek philosophical term for serene calmness of mind, freedom from anxiety.

clue.text: Gas and precious metal, given time, yield an old form of salt

parts.note: argon is a noble gas
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe: gas plus gold plus time makes an old kind of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' means an old sailor, not a chemical salt, despite the chemistry around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is a salt, and the Argonauts were the crew of Jason's ship in Greek myth, ancient seafarers.

clue.text: See around most of base that's in a bad way

indicators.note: around means the see wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

indicators.note: most of means drop the last letter

parts.note: base means vile, low or wicked

explanation.surface: Look around most of a military base that's in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese, not look: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something wickedly is acting in an evil manner; the adverb matches the phrase.
